full_name_ar: يزيد بن شجرة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9293) lists Yazid ibn Shajara (also ibn Abi Shajara) al-Rahawi, from the Raha tribe, whose companionship is disputed among scholars. It reports that Mu'awiya used to appoint him to command armies and records a sermon he gave.
research_evidence: عن يزيد بن شجرة، وكان من رها، وكان معاوية يستعمله على الجيوش، فخطبنا يوما
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: يزيد بن ثعلبة الأنصاري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9260) has a brief notice on Yazid ibn Tha'laba al-Ansari, quoting only Ibn Hibban's statement that he was a companion.
research_evidence: يزيد بن ثعلبة الأنصاري قال ابن حبّان: له صحبة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: يزيد بن عتر ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9311, Yazid ibn 'Amr al-Numayri, also called Yazid ibn al-Mu'tammil) quotes al-Mustaghfiri naming him Yazid ibn 'Itr al-Numayri, who came to the Prophet in a delegation. Al-Dulabi transmitted a hadith in which the delegation asked the Prophet for guidance and he taught them the pillars of Islam.
research_evidence: وقال المستغفري: يزيد بن عتر النميري وفد على النبيّ صلّى اللَّه عليه وآله وسلّم
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: يحيى بن هند ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba (entry 5519) lists Yahya ibn Hind ibn Haritha as a companion who witnessed al-Hudaybiya and the Pledge of Ridwan, citing Ibn Hibban. Abu Musa (al-Madini) recorded him in brief.
research_evidence: يحيى بن هند بن حارثة شهد الحديبية وبيعة الرضوان
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: يعيش بن طخفة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9386) quotes Ibn Sa'd that he was a Syrian whose hadith is transmitted by Egyptians. Via Ibn Lahi'a, al-Harith ibn Yazid and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr it records the story of the Prophet asking who would milk a camel and choosing Ya'ish after turning away men named Murra and Jamra. Ibn Hajar distinguishes him from another Ya'ish ibn Tikhfa who narrated from his father.
research_evidence: يعيش بن طخفة الغفاريّ قال ابن سعد: شامي، مخرج حديثه عن المصريين
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أبو ثعلبة الأشجعي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9669) quotes al-Bukhari, via Abu Ahmad al-Hakim, that he was a companion. His hadith, through Ibn Jurayj and 'Umar ibn Nabhan, concerns a man who lost two children in Islam and was promised Paradise by the Prophet; Ibn Mandah, Abu Hatim and al-Daraqutni discussed variant chains, some adding Abu Hurayra.
research_evidence: أبو ثعلبة الأشجعي قال البخاري: له صحبة، ذكره عنه الحاكم أبو أحمد وغيره
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أبو الدحداح الأنصاري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9867) calls him an ally of the Ansar whose name and lineage were not known. Through Anas, in Ahmad, al-Baghawi and al-Hakim, it records that he bought a disputed palm tree in exchange for his whole orchard and gave it away, and the Prophet repeatedly praised the palms he would have in Paradise.
research_evidence: أبو الدحداح الأنصاري حليف لهم
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أبو الرداد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9896) quotes Abu Ahmad al-Hakim and Ibn Hibban that Abu Raddad al-Laythi was a companion. His report on mercy (rahm) comes via al-Zuhri and Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Rahman and is found in Sunan Abi Dawud and Sahih Ibn Hibban.
research_evidence: أبو رداد الليثي قال أبو أحمد الحاكم وابن حبّان: له صحبة.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أبو نحيلة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 10645) discusses the spelling of his kunya (Abu Nuhayla, per al-Daraqutni) and describes him as a righteous man of Bajila. Via Ibn Ma'in and 'Ali ibn al-Madini it quotes Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna that he was a companion; Abu Hatim al-Razi disputed this.
research_evidence: هو رجل صالح من بجيلة حكاه الدّارقطنيّ، عن يحيى بن معين، وعن علي بن المديني- أن سفيان بن عيينة قال: إن أبا نحيلة له صحبة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أبو أذينة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9511) lists Abu Udhayna al-Sadafi of Egypt, who narrated a hadith from the Prophet about the qualities of women. Al-Baghawi said he did not know whether he was a companion, while Ibn al-Sakan counted him one among the Egyptians; the chain runs through Musa ibn 'Ali ibn Rabah from his father.
research_evidence: أبو أذينة: بمعجمة ونون مصغرا... من أهل مصر، روى عن النبي صلى اللَّه عليه وسلّم حديثا، ولا أدري له صحبة أم لا
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أبو حميضة المزني ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9801) notes that Ibn al-Sakan, al-'Uthmani and others listed Abu Humayda al-Muzani among the companions and Ibn Hibban affirmed his companionship. His hadith on eating etiquette was transmitted by Ibn al-Sakan and by al-Tabarani in Musnad al-Shamiyyin.
research_evidence: أبو حميضة المزني. ذكره ابن السّكن والعثمانيّ وغيرهما في الصحابة. وقال ابن حبان: له صحبة.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أبو سيلان ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 10076) says Ibn Hibban mentioned Abu Saylan among the companions in his kunya list, saying it is said he had companionship. Ibn Hajar suggests he may be 'Abdullah ibn Saylan, who has an earlier entry.
research_evidence: أبو سيلان: بكسر المهملة بعدها مثناة تحتانية
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أبو لاس الخزاعي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 10470) says his name is disputed, either 'Abdullah or Ziyad. He narrated a hadith about the Prophet mounting them on charity camels for Hajj, transmitted by 'Umar ibn al-Hakam and cited by al-Bukhari in his Sahih without full chain; al-Baghawi said he lived in Medina.
research_evidence: أبو لاس الخزاعي مختلف في اسمه، فقيل: عبد اللَّه، وقيل زياد.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أبو شيبة الأنصاري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 10115) records a report in which a masked man declares himself Abu Shayba al-Khudri, companion of the Messenger of God, and relates a hadith about entering Paradise; the narrator adds that he died and was buried on the spot. Abu Hatim al-Razi considered him and his father unknown.
research_evidence: من عرفني فأنا أبو شيبة الخدريّ صاحب رسول اللَّه
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أبو زهير بن معاذ ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9946) gives him as Abu Zuhayr ibn Mu'adh ibn Riyah al-Thaqafi. Abu Ahmad al-Hakim reports that Ibrahim al-Harbi counted him among companions known mainly by their kunya. His hadith is given by al-Tabarani under Mu'adh al-Thaqafi and by al-Mizzi under Abu Zuhayr al-Thaqafi.
research_evidence: أبو زهير بن معاذ بن رياح الثقفي
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أبو صخر العقيلي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 10138) says al-Bukhari, Muslim, Ibn Hibban and others listed Abu Sakhr al-'Uqayli among the companions, and gives his name as 'Abdullah ibn Qudama. It relates that he came to Medina and saw the Prophet with Abu Bakr and 'Umar speaking with a Jew who was reading the Torah about the Prophet's description.
research_evidence: أبو صخر العقيلي ذكره البخاريّ، ومسلم، وابن حبّان، وغيرهم في الصحابة.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أبو خيرة العبدي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9856m) traces his nisba to Subah ibn Lukayz of 'Abd al-Qays. Al-Bukhari, Khalifa, al-Dulabi, al-Tabarani and Abu Ahmad al-Hakim transmitted his account via Dawud ibn al-Musawir and Muqatil ibn Hammam: the 'Abd al-Qays delegation gave the Prophet arak (miswak) sticks and he prayed for forgiveness for the tribe.
research_students: Dawud ibn al-Musawir (via Muqatil ibn Hammam)
research_evidence: أبو خيرة العبديّ ثم الصّباحي نسبة إلى صباح، بضم المهملة وتخفيف الموحدة وآخره حاء مهملة- ابن لكيز بن أفصى
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أم إسحاق ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 11890) says the start of her hadith was given under her son Ishaq. The rest relates that she went in to the Prophet while he was making ablution and, weeping, told him that Ishaq, meaning her brother, had been killed.
research_evidence: أم إسحاق الغنوية: تقدم ذكر أول حديثها في ترجمة ولدها إسحاق في حرف الألف من الرّجال
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أم حبيبة مولاة ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 11969) lists Umm Habiba, freedwoman of Umm 'Atiyya, who narrated that she was among the women who escorted one of the Prophet's daughters as a bride.
research_evidence: أم حبيبة مولاة أم عطية ... كنت في النسوة اللاتي أهدين بعض بنات النبي صلّى اللَّه عليه وآله وسلّم
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أم عبد الله بنت أوس ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 12135) identifies her as the daughter of Aws al-Ansari and sister of Shaddad ibn Aws. It quotes Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr) that she was Syrian and that Damra ibn Habib narrated from her.
research_evidence: أم عبد الله بنت أوس الأنصاريّة، أخت شداد بن أوس الأنصاريّة. تقدم نسبها في ترجمته. قال أبو عمر: شامية
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أم قيس الهذلية ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 12216) quotes Abu Musa saying Ja'far listed her but narrated nothing from her. Ibn Hajar suspects she is the same as the preceding Umm Qays, reasoning that Ibn Mas'ud (a Hudhali) called the man who emigrated for Umm Qays 'a man from among us', so the Umm Qays who was proposed to may also have been Hudhali.
research_evidence: ١٢٢١٦- أم قيس الهذلية: قال أبو موسى: أوردها جعفر، ولم يخرج لها شيئا.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أم سفيان بنت الضحاك السلمية ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba lists Umm Sufyan bint al-Dahhak al-Sulamiyya as the maternal grandmother of Mansur ibn Safiyya, noting that Abu Musa mentioned her in his supplement. A second entry under the same name cites al-Mustaghfiri and Ibn al-Athir's view that it may be the same woman.
research_evidence: أم سفيان بنت الضحاك السلمية جدة منصور بن صفية يعني لأمه
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أم عامر بنت سويد ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 12126) says Abu Musa mentioned her in his supplement (al-Dhayl), citing al-Mustaghfiri, but recorded nothing from her. No further details are given.
research_evidence: ١٢١٢٦- أم عامر بنت سويد: ذكرها أبو موسى في الذّيل عن المستغفري، ولم يورد
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أم الغادية ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 12198) says she was already mentioned in the entry on Abu al-Ghadiya. It cites Ibn Manda and al-Khatib (al-Mu'talif) transmitting, through Tammam ibn Buzay', a report in which she went with a group to the Prophet and asked him for advice.
research_evidence: أم الغادية: تقدم ذكرها في ترجمة أبي الغادية، وأخرج ابن مندة والخطيب في المؤتلف من طريق تمام بن بزيع
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أم معبد مولاة ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 12265) describes her as the freedwoman of Qaraza ibn Ka'b al-Ansari and quotes Ibn Manda that her companionship is disputed. Ibn Manda cites a report via Musa ibn Muhammad al-Ansari in which she describes serving drinks to companions, and discusses the forbidden drinking vessels.
research_evidence: أم معبد مولاة قرظة بن كعب الأنصارية. قال ابن مندة: في صحبتها خلاف، وأورد من طريق موسى بن محمد الأنصاري

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن أبي حرام ( رضي الله عنه
generation: Mukhadram / Successor — lived in the Prophet's era but is not recorded as having met him
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 6609, in the section for names wrongly counted as companions) quotes Ibn al-Athir saying he saw this name in his own handwriting marked as found in three earlier companion books, but could not find it in them. Ibn Hajar says it is really the preceding entry, 'Abdullah ibn Umm Haram, with 'Umm' miswritten as 'Abi'.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 6622, in the section for names wrongly counted as companions) says Ibn 'Abd al-Barr treated him as different from 'Abdullah ibn Sa'd, paternal uncle of Haram ibn Hakim, but Ibn Hajar says they are one and the same person. full_name_ar: عبد الله البكري روت بنته بهية ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 4644; entry 5054 'Abdullah al-Bakri' cross-refers to it as Ibn Hurayth) quotes al-Bukhari that he was a companion. It quotes Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr) that his daughter Bahiyya narrated from him the hadith 'the best of deeds is performing ablution thoroughly', and cites Ibn Manda's chain for it.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 6799, in the section for names wrongly counted as companions) quotes Ibn Yunus that he was counted among the Ma'afir and took part in the conquest of Egypt. full_name_ar: يريم بن معديكرب بن أبرهة بن الصباح ( رضي الله عنه

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9410, third section of the letter Ya, for those who lived in the Prophet's era) says he lived in that era and had a son named al-Nadr. full_name_ar: يزيد أبو هانئ الحنفي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba fi Ma'rifat al-Sahaba (entry 5618) says his son Hani' narrated from him that his brother Qays ibn Ma'bad and his cousin Jariya ibn Zafar fought over a pasture, and Qays severed Jariya's hand; they took the case to the Prophet with Yazid present, and the Prophet ruled for Jariya to receive the blood-money for his hand from Qays's property. Ibn al-Athir adds that this Yazid Abu Hani' is the same person as Yazid ibn Ma'bad al-Hanafi, who came as a delegate to the Prophet with his brother Qays.
research_evidence: يزيد أبو هانئ الحنفي روى عَنْهُ ابنه هانئ، أَنَّهُ أخبره: أن أخاه قيس بن معبد، وجارية بن ظفر، وهو ابن عمه، اقتتلا
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: الأكثم بن ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba fi Ma'rifat al-Sahaba (entry 217, continuing on page 162) says he is also called Ibn Abi al-Jawn, that his name was 'Abd al-'Uzza ibn Munqidh, and traces his lineage to Rabi'a (Luhayy) ibn Haritha. It records the hadith, via Abu Hurayra, in which the Prophet told him he resembled 'Amr ibn Luhayy but that this would not harm him because he was a believer; it adds that the version mentioning the Dajjal is not authentic. He is described as the uncle of Sulayman ibn Surad al-Khuza'i, leader of the Tawwabun.
research_evidence: أكثم بْن الجون وقيل: ابن أَبِي الجون، واسمه: عبد العزى بْن منقذ بْن
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: بشر الغنوي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba fi Ma'rifat al-Sahaba (entry 437) gives his kunya as Abu 'Abdullah, says he is also called al-Khath'ami, and that his son 'Ubaydullah narrated from him. It cites, via Ahmad ibn Hanbal, his report that he heard the Prophet say Constantinople will be conquered, and 'how excellent its commander and that army'; the son relates that Maslama ibn 'Abd al-Malik asked him about it and then campaigned against Constantinople.
research_evidence: بشر الغنوي أَبُو عَبْد اللَّهِ وقيل: الخثعمي. روى عنه ابنه عُبَيْد اللَّهِ.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: تميم بن عبد عمرو ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba fi Ma'rifat al-Sahaba (entry 526) gives his kunya as Abu al-Hasan al-Mazini and says he was 'Ali ibn Abi Talib's governor over Medina when Sahl ibn Hunayf left to join 'Ali in Iraq, citing Abu Nu'aym from Ibn Ishaq. Via Ibn Shahin it traces his lineage to Mazin ibn al-Najjar.
research_evidence: تميم بْن عبد عمرو أَبُو الحسن المازني كان عاملًا لعلي بْن أَبِي طالب ﵁ عَلَى المدينة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: جرموز القريعي الضبعي الهجيمي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba fi Ma'rifat al-Sahaba (entry 718) says he was from Balhujaym ibn 'Amr ibn Tamim, also called al-Quray'i (another branch of Tamim), and that Abu Tamima al-Hujaymi narrated from him. It records his report that he asked the Prophet for advice and was told not to be one who curses.
research_evidence: جرموز الهجيمي من بلهجيم بْن عمرو بْن تميم. وقيل: القريعي، وهو بطن من تميم أيضًا. روى عنه أَبُو تميمة الهجيمي.

full_name_ar: خريم بن أوس ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba fi Ma'rifat al-Sahaba (entry 1438) traces his lineage to Tayy (al-Ta'i) and gives his kunya as Abu Laja'. It says he met the Prophet on his return from Tabuk and accepted Islam. In a report transmitted through his grandson Humayd ibn Minhab, he relates that he was present when al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib asked permission to recite poetry in praise of the Prophet.
research_evidence: خريم بْن أوس بْن حارثة بْن لام بن عمرو بْن طريف بْن عمرو بْن ثمامة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: ربيعة بن يزيد السلمي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 2641, heading on page 1088, text on page 1089) quotes al-Bukhari that he was a companion, while Ibn Hibban and al-'Askari report it only as 'it is said'. It quotes Ibn 'Abd al-Barr that he was among the Nawasib who reviled 'Ali, and Abu Hatim that nothing should be narrated from him and that listing him among the companions is baseless. Ibn Fathun, Abu 'Ali al-Ghassani and Ibn Mu'awwiz added him as supplements to Ibn 'Abd al-Barr, relying on al-Bukhari.
research_evidence: وقال ابن عبد البرّ في آخر ترجمة ربيعة الجرشي: أما ربيعة بن يزيد السلميّ فكان من النواصب يشتم عليّا.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: سنان بن عبد الله الجهني ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba fi Ma'rifat al-Sahaba (entry 2268) says he was a companion. It records, via Ibn 'Abbas, that his wife had him ask the Prophet whether she could perform Hajj on behalf of her mother who died without doing it, and the Prophet compared it to paying off a mother's debt. It notes that Abu Khalid al-Ahmar erred in one chain by calling him Sufyan ibn 'Abdullah.
research_evidence: سنان بْن عَبْد اللَّهِ الجهني له صحبة. روى أَبُو التياح الضبعي، عن موسى بْن سلمة الهذلي، عن ابن عباس
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: صفوان بن عبد الرحمن ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba fi Ma'rifat al-Sahaba (entry 2515) says his father brought him to the Prophet on the day of the Conquest of Mecca to pledge allegiance for hijra; the Prophet said there is no hijra after the Conquest, but al-'Abbas interceded and the Prophet accepted his pledge. It notes Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr) recorded his hadith with doubt over whether the name is Safwan ibn 'Abd al-Rahman or 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Safwan.
research_evidence: صفوان بْن عبد الرحمن بْن صفوان، القرشي الجمحي. أتى به أبوه النَّبِيّ ﷺ يَوْم الفتح ليبايعه عَلَى الهجرة

full_name_ar: صرد بن عبد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 4080) calls him al-Azdi and quotes Ibn Hibban that he was from Jurash and a companion. It cites Ibn Ishaq's al-Maghazi that he came to the Prophet with the Azd delegation, accepted Islam, and was put in charge of the Muslims of his people to fight the neighbouring polytheists. It quotes al-Waqidi that when the Prophet died, his governor over Jurash was Surad ibn 'Abdullah al-Azdi.
research_evidence: صرد بن عبد اللَّه الأزديّ. قال ابن حبّان: جرشي، له صحبة.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن سفيان الأزدي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 4740, continuing on page 1843) says he settled in Homs. It notes al-Bukhari and Ibn al-Sakan listed him among the companions and Abu Hatim and Ibn Hibban affirmed his companionship. Al-Tabarani recorded a hadith from him about fasting in the path of God, and Ibn Fathun noted that Ibn Mufarrij wrongly gave his name as 'Abdullah ibn Shaqir.
research_evidence: ٤٧٤٠ ز- عبد اللَّه بن سفيان الأزدي: نزيل حمص.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن جراد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 4606) gives his lineage as al-'Amiri al-'Uqayli following Ibn Makula, and notes an alternative lineage given by Ya'la ibn al-Ashdaq. It says al-Bukhari, Ibn Hibban and Ya'qub ibn Sufyan counted him as a companion, and Ibn Manda placed him among the people of Ta'if. Ya'la ibn al-Ashdaq and Abu Qatada al-Shami narrated from him.
research_evidence: ٤٦٠٦- عبد الله بن جراد بن المنتفق بن عامر بن عقيل العامري العقيلي. نسبه ابن ماكولا.

full_name_ar: ضمام بن ثعلبة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 4198, Dimam ibn Tha'laba al-Sa'di) says he was from Banu Sa'd ibn Bakr and appears in Anas's hadith in the two Sahihs, where a Bedouin came asking for the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib, accepted Islam, and declared himself the envoy of his people. It quotes 'Umar ibn al-Khattab that he never saw anyone ask better or more concisely than Dimam, and al-Baghawi that he lived in Kufa.
research_evidence: وفيه: أنه أسلم، وقال: أنا رسول من ورائي من قومي، وأنا ضمام بن ثعلبة.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن عبد المدان ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 4818) gives his lineage in Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b (al-Harithi). Ibn Hibban says he was a companion, and Ibn Sa'd and al-Tabari say he came as a delegate to the Prophet; Ibn al-Kalbi says his name was 'Abd al-Hajar and the Prophet changed it. Wathima reports he urged his people not to apostatise after the Prophet's death, and it is said he lived until 'Ali's caliphate and was killed by Busr ibn Abi Artat when he raided Yemen for Mu'awiya.
research_evidence: ٤٨١٨- عبد اللَّه بن عبد المدان: واسمه عمرو بن الديّان، واسمه يزيد بن قطن بن الحارث بن مالك بن ربيعة بن كعب بن الحارث الحارثي.

full_name_ar: الفراسي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba fi Ma'rifat al-Sahaba (entry 4211) says he was from Banu Firas ibn Malik ibn Kinana and that his hadith was held by the people of Egypt. It cites, via Abu Dawud, his son Ibn al-Firasi reporting that he asked the Prophet whether he should beg from people, and the Prophet said no, but if he must ask, he should ask the righteous.

full_name_ar: ياسر بن سويد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba fi Ma'rifat al-Sahaba (entry 5502) calls him Yasir ibn Suwayd al-Juhani, father of Musri', and says his hadith was preserved by his descendants. It relates that the Prophet sent him with a cavalry troop while his wife was pregnant; when the child was born she brought him to the Prophet, who prayed over him and named him Musri' because he had 'hastened into Islam'. Recorded by Ibn Manda and Abu Nu'aym.
research_evidence: ياسر بن سويد الجهني والد مسرع. حديثه عند أولاده.

full_name_ar: عامر بن سعد بن عمرو ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 4404) lists 'Amir ibn Sa'd ibn 'Amr, an Ansari of the Aws, who is said to have fought at Badr. It cites al-'Adawi and Ibn al-Qaddah as recording him, and notes Ibn al-Dabbagh added him in his supplement. No death date is given.
research_evidence: ٤٤٠٤- عامر بن سعد بن عمرو ... الأنصاري الأوسي ... شهد بدرا فيما يقال

full_name_ar: علي بن الحكم السلمي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 5699) lists 'Ali ibn al-Hakam al-Sulami, brother of Mu'awiya ibn al-Hakam. Al-Bukhari, al-Tabarani, Ibn al-Sakan and Ibn Manda recorded a report through Kathir ibn Mu'awiya ibn al-Hakam: his horse struck the wall of the trench and injured a man's leg, the Prophet recited 'In the name of Allah' over it, and the pain went away. Ibn Manda called the report rare (gharib), known only through this chain.
research_evidence: ٥٦٩٩- علي بن الحكم السلمي ... أخو معاوية بن الحكم وإخوته

full_name_ar: أبو طريف الهذلي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 10164) says al-Baghawi, Mutayyin, Ibn Hibban, Ibn al-Sakan and others counted Abu Tarif al-Hudhali among the companions, and that he was present at the siege of al-Ta'if. Ibn Qani' gave his name as Kaysan, while Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr) said Sinan. Ahmad and al-Hasan ibn Sufyan transmitted his report through Zakariyya ibn Ishaq from al-Walid ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Sumayra.
research_evidence: ١٠١٦٤- أبو طريف الهذلي ... ذكره البغويّ، ومطيّن، وابن حبّان، وابن السّكن وغيرهم في الصحابة، وشهد حصار الطائف

full_name_ar: محمد بن فضالة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7816) says Muhammad ibn Fadala is the same person as Anas ibn Fadala, who has an earlier entry. That earlier entry (273, page 259) gives him as Anas ibn Fadala ibn 'Adi ibn Haram al-Ansari al-Zafari and quotes Abu Hatim ('he had companionship') and al-Bukhari (he and his father were companions of the Prophet). No death date is given.
research_evidence: ٧٨١٦- محمد بن فضالة ... هو أنس بن فضالة- تقدم أيضا
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: مخول بن يزيد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7866) lists Mikhwal ibn Yazid al-Sulami al-Bahzi, who according to Ibn al-Sakan lived in Mecca. Abu Ya'la transmitted, through his son al-Qasim ibn Mikhwal, a report that the Prophet settled a dispute over a gazelle caught in snares near al-Abwa' and told him to pray, give alms, and perform hajj and umra. The chain through Ibn Masmul is described as weak, and Ibn al-Sakan says this is his only report.
research_evidence: ٧٨٦٦- مخول بن يزيد ... السلميّ، ثم البهزيّ. قال ابن السّكن: وهو ممن سكن مكة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عامر بن عمرو المزني ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 4428) lists 'Amir ibn 'Amr al-Muzani, father of Hilal, whose companionship several scholars accepted. His son Hilal reported from him seeing the Prophet preach at Mina on a white mule, with debate over whether Hilal heard it directly or through his uncle Rafi' ibn 'Amr; versions appear in Ahmad and Abu Dawud. A hadith on begging attributed to him is judged a mistake for 'A'idh ibn 'Amr.
research_evidence: ٤٤٢٨- عامر بن عمرو المزنيّ، والد هلال
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أبو مجيبة الباهلي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 10506) lists Abu Mujiba, father (or uncle) of Mujiba al-Bahiliyya, and says he lived in Basra. It notes some gave his name as 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith, and that Mujiba was in fact a woman ('an old woman of her people'). He appears in chains in Ibn Majah and Ibn Abi Dawud; Ibn Hibban counted him among the companions, while Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr) said he did not know him.
research_evidence: ١٠٥٠٦- أبو مجيبة ... أبو مجيبة أو عمها سكن البصرة

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7690) lists Malik ibn 'Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i as a companion of the Ashja' tribe. It notes he is mentioned in the entry on Salim ibn 'Awf and was recorded by Abu Musa (al-Madini). No other details or death date are given.

full_name_ar: محرز بن زهير ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7761) lists Muhriz ibn Zuhayr (also given as Ibn Zahr) al-Aslami, of the Aslam tribe, whose companionship al-Bukhari affirmed. A slave woman of his transmitted his saying 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the time of liars.' Abu Nu'aym noted the variant spellings of his father's name, and the footnotes cite al-Thiqat, al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil, Usd al-Ghaba and al-Isti'ab.
research_evidence: محرز بن زهير ويقال ابن زهر الأسلمي ... رجل من أسلم، وكان من أصحاب النبي صلّى اللَّه عليه وآله وسلم

full_name_ar: أنيس بن مرثد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 281, under Anas ibn Abi Marthad al-Ghanawi) says Ibn Hibban and Ibn 'Abd al-Barr called him Anis, while al-Baghawi treated Anis ibn Marthad ibn Abi Marthad as a separate person. Citing Ibn Sa'd, it says he was the Prophet's scout at Awtas, had the kunya Abu Yazid, and died in the year 20.

full_name_ar: إياس بن عبد الله ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 380) lists Iyas ibn 'Abdullah, also called Ibn 'Abd al-Fihri, with the kunya Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, by which he is best known; his main entry is in the kunya section. The footnotes cite Ibn Hibban's al-Thiqat, Tajrid Asma' al-Sahaba and al-Isti'ab.
research_evidence: ٣٨٠- إياس بن عبد اللَّه ... ويقال ابن عبد الفهري. أبو عبد الرحمن. مشهور بكنيته.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أفلح بن أبي القعيس ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 227) lists him as Aflah, brother of Abu al-Qu'ays, the foster (milk) uncle of 'A'isha. Ibn Manda counted him among Banu Sulaym, while Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr) suggested an Ash'ari affiliation. His story is transmitted via Malik from al-Zuhri from 'Urwa from 'A'isha and appears in the two Sahihs. No death date is given.
research_evidence: ٢٢٧- أفلح أخو أبي القعيس
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أنيف بن صلة الجذامي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 303) lists him as Anif ibn Milla al-Judhami (this edition spells the father's name ملة rather than صلة). It says he was a companion who lived in al-Ramla and died at Bayt Jibrin in Palestine. Ibn Hibban counted him among the companions, and Ibn al-Sakan noted Ibn Ishaq listed him among the Judham delegation to the Prophet.
research_evidence: أنيف بن ملة الجذامي، من بني الضيب، له صحبة سكن الرّملة، ومات ببيت جبرين من كورة فلسطين
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: الأسلع السعدي رجل من ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entries 122-123) covers al-Asla' al-A'raji, of Banu al-A'raj ibn Ka'b, also given as al-Asla' ibn Sharik al-A'raji al-Tamimi; Ibn Hajar treats the two headings as the same person, while Ibn 'Abd al-Barr distinguished two men. His report is linked to the revelation of tayammum, and al-Rabi' ibn Badr transmitted his hadith. Sources cited are Usd al-Ghaba and al-Isti'ab.
research_evidence: ١٢٢- الأسلع الأعرجي ... روى حديثه الربيع بن بدر
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: الأخرم والد عبد الله ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 57) lists al-Akhram al-Hujaymi as a companion recognised by several scholars. He is known through a report transmitted by his son 'Abdullah ibn al-Akhram, in which the Prophet said of the Day of Dhu Qar that it was the first day the Arabs got even (with the Persians). Ibn Hajar notes debate over whether he should be distinguished from others named al-Akhram.
research_evidence: ٥٧- الأخرم الهجيمي ... عن عبد اللَّه بن الأخرم، عن أبيه
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: الأقعس بن سلمة عداده ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 236) says al-Aq'as ibn Salama was counted among the people of al-Yamamah and had companionship. It notes Ibn Hibban also called him al-Aqisar ibn Salama al-Hanafi, and that al-Baghawi transmitted a hadith through him. No death date is given.
research_evidence: الأقعس بن سلمة ... عداده في أهل اليمامة، له صحبة

full_name_ar: بشر بن عاصم يقال ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 663) lists Bishr ibn 'Asim, who served as an official (governor) under the caliph 'Umar. Ibn Hajar records variant attributions from al-Bukhari, Ibn Hibban and Ibn al-Sakan, some calling him al-Thaqafi and others al-Makhzumi, and flags one addition to his lineage as an error. No death date is given.
research_evidence: ٦٦٣ ز- بشر بن عاصم ... عامل عمر.

full_name_ar: بشير بن معبد الأسلمي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 705) lists Bashir ibn Ma'bad, Abu Ma'bad al-Aslami, a companion counted among the people of Kufa who is said to have witnessed the Pledge of al-Ridwan. His son Bishr ibn Bashir transmitted from him, and his grandson Muhammad ibn Bishr passed on his reports. Ibn Hajar notes that Ibn Hibban split him into two entries but argues they are the same man, citing al-Bukhari, Ibn Manda, Ibn al-Sakan and al-Baghawi.
research_evidence: ٧٠٥- بشير بن معبد، أبو معبد الأسلمي ... له صحبة، عداده في أهل الكوفة

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 1090) lists Jubayr ibn al-Hubab ibn al-Mundhir al-Ansari. It quotes Ibn Hibban that he is said to have had companionship, though the chain is questionable. Mutayyin listed him among the companions, and 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Rafi' named him among those who fought with 'Ali at Siffin; al-Tabarani, Ibn Manda and Abu Nu'aym also reported him.

full_name_ar: جحش الجهني والد عبد ( رضي الله عنه
generation: Mukhadram / Successor — lived in the Prophet's era but is not recorded as having met him
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists Jahsh al-Juhani, father of 'Abdullah, in its fourth section (people listed as companions by mistake), entry 1331. He explains that al-Tabarani counted him as a companion because of a corrupted chain from Ibn Ishaq, reading 'Abdullah ibn Jahsh al-Juhani where Abu Dawud and others have 'Abdullah ibn Unays al-Juhani. So in Ibn Hajar's view no companion of this name existed. A separate short entry (1109) quotes Ibn Fathun that al-Tabari mentioned a Jahsh al-Juhani among the companions.
research_evidence: ١٣٣١- جحش الجهني ... عن عبد اللَّه بن جحش الجهنيّ، عن أبيه
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: الحارث بن خزيمة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 1404) gives al-Harith ibn Khazama (Khuzayma) ibn 'Adi, an Ansari of Khazraj descent, who fought at Badr and later battles. It says he died in Medina in the year 40 at age 67. It also mentions his role, reported by al-Tabari and in the hadith collections, in bringing Qur'anic verses to 'Umar.

full_name_ar: الحارث بن مسلم القرشي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 1488) lists al-Harith ibn Muslim al-Hijazi, Abu al-Mughira al-Makhzumi (Makhzum is a clan of Quraysh). It quotes al-Bukhari, and also Ibn Abi Hatim, that he was a companion; Ibn al-Dabbagh and Ibn Fathun also included him. No narrators or death date are given.

full_name_ar: حبيب بن حماز وقد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Habib bin Hammaz al-Asadi is entry 1580 in Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (vol. 2, p. 15), where Abu Musa, citing Abdan, counts him among the Companions who travelled with the Prophet, citing a report via al-A'mash from Amr bin Murra from Abdullah bin al-Harith. Ibn Hajar notes others narrate it as Habib from Abu Dharr, and that al-Bukhari, Abu Hatim, al-Daraqutni and Ibn Hibban list him among the Tabi'un. No death year is given.

full_name_ar: حرملة بن إياس العنبري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 1671; entry 1667 'Harmala bin Iyas' cross-refers here) names him Harmala bin Abdullah bin Iyas (or bin Aws) al-Anbari, who settled in Basra; Abu Hatim and Ibn Hibban affirm his companionship. His son Ulayba narrated from him, and his hadith appears in al-Bukhari's al-Adab al-Mufrad and the Musnad of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi with a sound (hasan) chain. He is sometimes named after his grandfather as Harmala bin Iyas; al-Baghawi treated them as two men, which al-Dhahabi rejected. No death year is given.
research_evidence: حرملة: بن عبد اللَّه بن إياس . وقيل ابن أوس العنبريّ. نزل البصرة. وقال أبو حاتم: له صحبة.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: حنظلة بن حنيفة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 1860) names him Hanzala bin Hidhyam bin Hanifa al-Tamimi, also called al-Asadi (of Asad Khuzayma) and al-Maliki, and states that he, his father and his grandfather Hanifa were all Companions. Ibn Hajar notes that al-Uqayli gave the name inverted as 'Hanzala bin Hanifa bin Hidhyam', and that al-Bukhari reported this inversion from some narrators. The entry cites a hadith via Imam Ahmad. No death year is given.
research_evidence: حنظلة بن حذيم: بن حنيفة التميمي ويقال الأسديّ أسد خزيمة. ... وقد قال فيه العقيلي في رواية حنظلة بن حنيفة بن حذيم فقلبه.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: حي الليثي له صحبة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 1904) names him Huyayy bin Haram al-Laythi; Yunus in Tarikh Misr lists him among the Companions and Ibn al-Sakan says he had companionship and is counted among the Egyptians, adding that his hadith is questionable. Via Ibn Lahi'a, Abu Tamim (spelled al-Haysamani on the page) reports that Huyayy al-Laythi, a Companion of the Prophet, would pray Zuhr at home once the sun declined and then pray again with the congregation if he found them. Al-Quda'i in al-Khitat says he is said to have had companionship.
research_evidence: حيي: بتحتانيتين مصغّرا- ابن حرام الليثي. ... وقال ابن السّكن: له صحبة. عداده في المصريين
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: حنيفة أبو حذيم يقال ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 1876) names him Hanifa bin Jubayr bin Bakr bin Hayy bin Sa'd bin Tha'laba bin Zayd Manat bin Tamim al-Tamimi, grandfather of Hanzala bin Hidhyam, and refers to the entry on Hanzala. In that entry (1860) Ibn Hajar states that Hanzala, his father Hidhyam and his grandfather Hanifa were all Companions. No death year is given.
research_evidence: حنيفة: بفتح أوله، ابن جبير بن بكر بن حيّ بن سعد بن ثعلبة بن زيد مناة بن تميم التميميّ، جدّ حنظلة بن حذيم

full_name_ar: خالد بن أبي جيل ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 2157) names him Khalid bin Jabal (in al-Bukhari's and Ibn al-Barqi's version 'Jayl'), al-Adwani al-Ta'ifi; the chain also calls him Khalid bin Abi Jabal. Ibn al-Sakan says he lived in Ta'if, has a single hadith, and is said to have pledged allegiance under the tree. His hadith, transmitted by his son Abd al-Rahman and recorded by Ahmad and Ibn Abi Shayba, describes seeing the Prophet in the east of Thaqif's territory, standing on a bow or staff, when he came to them seeking support. No death year is given.
research_students: Abd al-Rahman bin Khalid bin Abi Jabal
research_evidence: خالد: بن جبل بفتح الجيم والموحدة، وقع في رواية البخاريّ وابن البرقي: جيل، بكسر الجيم بعدها تحتانية ساكنة ... العدوانيّ، بفتح المهملتين، الطائفي.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: خويلد بن بجير من ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 2307) names him Khuwaylid bin Khalid bin Bujayr bin Amr bin Hammas al-Kinani, Abu Aqrab, grandfather of Abu Nawfal bin Abi Amr bin Abi Aqrab (some say there is no one between Abu Nawfal and Abu Aqrab). Al-Tabarani, Ibn Shahin and Ibn Hibban list him among the Companions; it is also said he is Khalid bin Bujayr. No death year is given.
research_evidence: خويلد: بن خالد بن بجير ، بالجيم مصغرا، ابن عمرو بن حماس- بكسر أوله والتخفيف والإهمال- الكناني، أبو عقرب
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: خلاد بن السائب الأنصاري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 2282) gives his lineage as Khallad bin al-Sa'ib bin Khallad bin Suwayd bin Tha'laba al-Ansari al-Khazraji. Ibn al-Sakan says he had companionship, and others say both he and his father did, as stated in the narration of Muslim bin Abi Maryam from Ata bin Yasar from Khallad, a hadith recorded by Abu Nu'aym. No death year is given.
research_evidence: خلاد بن السّائب بن خلاد بن سويد بن ثعلبة بن عمرو بن حارثة بن امرئ القيس الأنصاري الخزرجي. قال ابن السّكن: له صحبة.

full_name_ar: الخرقاء هي السوداء التي ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (women's section, entry 11095) identifies Kharqa' as the black woman who used to sweep the Prophet's Mosque. She is mentioned in a report of Hammad bin Zayd from Thabit from Anas; Ibn Manda listed her this way and Abu Nu'aym followed him. No death year is given.
research_evidence: خرقاء: المرأة السوداء التي كانت تقمّ المسجد النبوي. لها ذكر من رواية حماد بن زيد، عن ثابت، عن أنس.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: ديلم بن هوشع الحميري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 2415) calls Daylam al-Himyari (also Daylam bin Abi Daylam, bin Fayruz, or bin Husha') a well-known Companion who asked the Prophet about drinks and other matters, then settled in Egypt, where its people narrated from him. Ibn Yunus gives his lineage as Daylam bin Husha' bin Sa'd bin Abi Janab bin Mas'ud, traced to Jayshan, and says he was the first delegate to reach the Prophet from Yemen, sent from Mu'adh bin Jabal, and that he took part in the conquest of Egypt. Abu al-Khayr Marthad narrated from him.
research_evidence: ديلم الحميري: وهو ديلم بن أبي ديلم، ويقال ديلم بن فيروز، ويقال ديلم بن هوشع، صحابيّ مشهور
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: ذواليدين صلي مع النبي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 2487) lists Dhu al-Yadayn al-Sulami, said to be al-Khirbaq, though Ibn Hibban treated them as two people. Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet prayed one of the afternoon prayers and gave the salam after two rak'as, whereupon a man with long hands called Dhu al-Yadayn asked whether the prayer had been shortened or he had forgotten; al-Bukhari and Muslim both record it via Ibn Sirin from Abu Hurayra. No death year is given.
research_evidence: ذو اليدين السّلمي: يقال هو الخرباق. وفرّق بينهما ابن حبّان

full_name_ar: رزين بن أنس يقال ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 2657) names him Razin bin Anas bin Amir al-Sulami; Ibn Hibban says he is said to have had companionship and Ibn al-Sakan affirms it. Abu Ya'la, Ibn al-Sakan and al-Tabarani record, via Fahd bin Awf from Na'il bin Mutarrif bin Razin from his father from his grandfather, that Razin came to the Prophet fearing others would seize his people's well, and the Prophet wrote him a document. No death year is given.
research_evidence: رزين: براء وزاي، بوزن عظيم، ابن أنس بن عامر، سلمي قال ابن حبان: يقال إن له صحبة.

full_name_ar: رجاء امرأة روى عنها ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (women's section, entry 11174) lists Raja' al-Ghanawiyya. Ibn Sirin narrated from her that she was with the Prophet when a woman who had lost three children asked him to pray for her son, and he called such loss 'a fortified shield' (from Hellfire). Ahmad recorded it via Abd al-Razzaq from Hisham from Ibn Sirin, and Ibn Hajar calls its narrators trustworthy. No death year is given.
research_evidence: رجاء الغنوية. روى ابن سيرين عن امرأة يقال لها رجاء أنها قالت: كنت عند النبي صلّى اللَّه عليه وسلّم

full_name_ar: زيد بن مريع الأنصاري ( رضي الله عنه

possible_duplicate_of.core_famous: Umm Thabit bint Haritha bin Zayd

bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba fi Ma'rifat al-Sahaba (entry 1872) names him Zayd bin Mirba' bin Qayzi al-Ansari of Banu Haritha, counted among the people of the Hijaz; Salih bin Ahmad bin Hanbal and Ibn Ma'in state that Ibn Mirba's name was Zayd. Yazid bin Shayban al-Azdi reports that Ibn Mirba' came to them at Arafat bearing a message from the Prophet about the pilgrimage stations. The entry says he and his brothers Abdullah, Abd al-Rahman and Murara were Companions; Ibn Manda and Abu Nu'aym recorded him.
research_evidence: د ع: زيد بْن مربع بْن قيظي الأنصاري من بني حارثة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: زيد بن أبي أوفي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 2885) names him Zayd bin Abi Awfa al-Aslami, brother of Abdullah bin Abi Awfa, as Ibn Hibban states. Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hasan bin Sufyan and al-Bukhari (al-Tarikh al-Saghir) record his hadith about entering the Medina mosque while the Prophet gathered his Companions, on the Prophet's pairing of Companions in brotherhood. Ibn al-Sakan says none of its three chains is sound, and al-Bukhari says the narrators' hearing from one another is unknown. No death year is given.
research_evidence: زيد بن أبي أوفى : بن خالد بن الحارث بن أبي أسيد بن رفاعة بن ثعلبة بن هوازن بن أسلم الأسلمي، أخو عبد اللَّه

full_name_ar: زيد بن كعب السلمي ( رضي الله عنه

possible_duplicate_of.core_famous: Ka'b bin Zayd bin Qays bin Malik

bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba fi Ma'rifat al-Sahaba (entry 1866) names him Zayd bin Ka'b al-Sulami al-Bahzi, the man of the wounded wild ass, named as such by al-Baghawi and others, who gave it as a gift to the Prophet. The report, via Yazid bin Harun from Yahya bin Sa'id from Muhammad bin Ibrahim from Isa bin Talha from Umayr bin Salama al-Damri from al-Bahzi, tells of the Prophet on his way to Mecca finding a wounded wild ass in a valley of al-Rawha'. Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 2937) also lists him. No death year is given.

full_name_ar: سعد بن عمارة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba fi Ma'rifat al-Sahaba (entry 2023) names him Sa'd bin Umara (or Umara bin Sa'd), Abu Sa'id al-Zuraqi, better known by his kunya; most authorities call him Sa'd bin Umara. Narrators from him include Abdullah bin Murra, Abdullah bin Abi Bakr, Sulayman bin Habib al-Muharibi and Yahya bin Sa'id al-Ansari, and one of his reports concerns a man of Ashja' asking the Prophet about coitus interruptus. Abu Nu'aym, Abu Umar and Abu Musa recorded him. No death year is given.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3247, among the unattributed men named Sa'd) lists Sa'd, father of al-Harith. Ibn Hajar quotes Ibn Hibban's book on the Companions, which says his kunya was Abu al-Mutarrif and that he had companionship. No lineage or death year is given.
research_evidence: سعد: أبو الحارث. قال ابن حبّان في «الصّحابة» : يكنى أبا المطرف، وله صحبة.

full_name_ar: سعد بن أبي ذئاب ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3157) lists Sa'd bin Abi Dhubab al-Dawsi (spelled Dhubab on the page); Ibn Hibban affirms his companionship. Ahmad and Ibn Abi Shayba record his report that he came to the Prophet, accepted Islam, and was appointed over his own people, who kept the property they had when they became Muslim; it includes a story with Umar about zakat on honey. Al-Baghawi says he knows no other hadith from him. No death year is given.

The reports about him, including the account of his conversion, are transmitted by Abd al-Hamid bin Yazid bin Salama. Ibn Manda and Abu Nu'aym recorded him. No death year is given.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3601) lists him as Sawada (the name with an added 'ha') bin al-Rabi' al-Jarmi; al-Bukhari says he had companionship and is counted among the Basrans. Ahmad records via Salm bin Abd al-Rahman that Sawada came to the Prophet, who ordered him a few camels and told him to have his children feed their young animals well and trim their nails. No death year is given.

full_name_ar: سليط بن عمرو العامري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3435) names him Salit bin Amr bin Abd Shams al-Amiri, brother of al-Sakran bin Amr, who accepted Islam early, before Umar. Ibn Ishaq lists him among the emigrants to Abyssinia and among the Prophet's envoys to kings, sent to Hawdha bin Ali, chief of al-Yamama; al-Waqidi and Abu Ma'shar count him among the people of Badr. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn al-Kalbi list him among those martyred at al-Yamama; no year is stated.
research_evidence: سليط بن عمرو بن عبد شمس العامريّ. تقدم نسبه في الّذي قبله، وتقدم ذكر أخيه السّكران بن عمرو قريبا، وأسلم سليط قديما قبل عمر.
dod_s: Died at: Battle of al-Yamama — 12 AH (some sources: 11 AH) / c. 633 CE (year of the event)

full_name_ar: سعر بن شعبة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: The Hadith Transmitters Encyclopedia page for Sa'r ibn Shu'ba, Abu Jabir al-Du'ali, quotes Ibn Hibban's al-Thiqat. The entry begins with his own report mentioning a collector (musaddiq) of the Messenger of God coming while he was in one of the mountain tracks. No death year is given.

She prayed with the Prophet towards both qiblas and gave the women's pledge; she reported the Prophet explaining that 'betraying husbands' in the pledge meant taking a husband's wealth to give to someone else.
research_evidence: سلمى بنت قيس بن عمرو بن عبيد بن مالك بن عدي بن عامر بن غنم ابن عدي بن النجار الأنصارية النجارية ... تكنى أم المنذر، وهي بكنيتها أشهر

full_name_ar: شريك بن طارق الحنظلي ( رضي الله عنه

Al-Waqidi, Khalifa ibn Khayyat and Ibn Sa'd list him among the companions who settled in Kufa.

full_name_ar: شريح الذي روى عنه ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 3910) lists this Shurayh with no known lineage. It quotes Abu Umar (Ibn Abd al-Barr) that Wasil al-Ahdab narrated from Abu Wa'il from Shurayh, a companion, the hadith qudsi 'O son of Adam, walk to Me and I will run to you'. Abu Umar says he does not know whether he is one of the other companions named Shurayh.
research_evidence: روى واصل الأحدب، عن أبي وائل، عن شريح- رجل من أصحاب رسول اللَّه صلّى اللَّه عليه وسلم

full_name_ar: شهاب الجرمي أبو كليب ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3953, Shihab ibn al-Majnun al-Jarmi) quotes Ibn Hibban and al-Baghawi that Shihab al-Jarmi, grandfather of Asim ibn Kulayb, had companionship; Ibn al-Sakan says his hadith is among the Kufans and he is not well known as a companion. Al-Tirmidhi and others record via Asim ibn Kulayb from his father from his grandfather that he saw the Prophet pointing with his index finger and saying 'O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm on Your religion'; al-Tirmidhi calls it gharib. Al-Tabarani gives variant names Shabib and Shutayr.
research_evidence: قال ابن حبّان والبغويّ: شهاب الجرمي جدّ عاصم بن كليب، له صحبة

full_name_ar: صخر بن وديعة الغامدي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (al-Mizzi) lists him as Sakhr ibn Wada'a al-Ghamidi, a Hijazi companion who settled in Taif. He narrated from the Prophet the hadith 'O Allah, bless my community in its early mornings', and his hadith is recorded by the four Sunan authors.

full_name_ar: الضحاك بن أبي جبيرة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 4180) calls him al-Ansari and quotes Ibn Hibban that he had companionship. Ibn Mandah records via al-Sha'bi from him the hadith 'I and the Hour were sent like these two', pointing with two fingers. Ibn Hajar says citing him for the occasion of revelation of 'Do not insult one another by nicknames' (49:11) reverses the name, and the correct form is Abu Jabira ibn al-Dahhak.

full_name_ar: ضمرة بن سعد السلمي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 4206) heads the entry Damra ibn Rabi'a al-Sulami but says he is also called Damra ibn Sa'd, the better-known form, or Dumayra. Al-Bukhari and Ibn al-Sakan say he had companionship, al-Baghawi says he lived in Medina, and Ibn Mandah says both he and his father Sa'd were companions.

full_name_ar: أبو عمرة عبد الله ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 10304, Abu 'Amra al-Ansari) records disagreement over his name: Bashir, Tha'laba ibn 'Amr ibn Mihsan of Banu Malik ibn al-Najjar, or (per Ibn al-Kalbi) 'Amr ibn Mihsan. It mentions his grandson Yahya ibn Tha'laba ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi 'Amra, and that Musa ibn 'Uqba held Tha'laba to be his brother.
research_evidence: وقيل اسمه ثعلبة بن عمرو بن محصن بن عمرو بن عبيد بن عمرو بن مبذول بن مالك بن النجار
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أبو خيثمة اسمه عبد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9853) lists Abu Khaythama al-Ansari al-Salimi, who appears in Ka'b ibn Malik's long account of his repentance: at Tabuk a figure was seen approaching through the mirage and turned out to be Abu Khaythama. Al-Waqidi gives his name as Abdullah ibn Khaythama, while others name him Malik ibn Qays; Ibn Hajar leaves the question open.
research_evidence: وقد قال الواقديّ: إن اسم أبي خيثمة هذا عبد اللَّه بن خيثمة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن طخفة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba treats him within the entry (4315) for his father Tahfa, also spelled Tikhfa or Tighfa, ibn Qays al-Ghifari; al-Bukhari preferred the form Tikhfa. The entry says some hold that the companionship belongs to the son, Abdullah ibn Tahfa/Tikhfa, and that he is the one in the story; the father's hadith is recorded by Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah and Ibn Hibban. (Tahdhib al-Kamal, shamela 3722/6757, says Tikhfa's single hadith concerns the prohibition of sleeping on the stomach.) Isaba's separate entry 4789 for Abdullah ibn Tahfa only refers to this entry.
research_evidence: طهفة ويقال طخفة بالخاء المعجمة ... بن قيس الغفاريّ. صحابيّ ... ويقال: إن الصّحبة لابنه عبد اللَّه بن طهفة، وأنه صاحب القصّة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن هلال الثقفي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba lists him as Abdullah ibn Hilal ibn Abdullah ibn Hammam al-Thaqafi. Al-Bazzar and others count him among the companions and Ibn Hibban says he had companionship; al-Baghawi says he lived in Mecca. Al-Bukhari mentioned him among the companions but withheld judgment because he did not explicitly state he heard from the Prophet.
research_evidence: عبد اللَّه بن هلال بن عبد اللَّه بن همّام الثقفي. ذكره جماعة منهم البزّار في الصحابة. وقال ابن حبان: له صحبة

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن هلال الأنصاري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 4823) lists him as 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd (also given as 'Abdullah ibn 'Abdullah ibn Hilal or 'Abdullah ibn Hilal) al-Ansari, of the people of Quba. It quotes Ibn Abi Hatim that his mawla Bishr narrated from him, and Ibn Hibban that he was a companion. A report in al-Tabarani describes his hair and beard staying white and his night prayer and daytime fasting after the Prophet blessed him.
research_evidence: من أهل قباء. قال ابن أبي حاتم: روى عنه مولاه بشر. قال أبو نعيم: يقال: عبد اللَّه بن عبد اللَّه بن هلال.

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن ثابت الأنصاري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 4591) quotes Ibn Hibban that he had companionship and al-Bukhari that his hadith is not sound. Ahmad records via Jabir al-Ju'fi from al-Sha'bi from him a report about Umar ibn al-Khattab coming to the Prophet. A second entry (4592) names an Abdullah ibn Thabit al-Ansari described as the Prophet's servant, possibly the same man; Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mandah treated them as two people.

full_name_ar: عبد الرحمن بن صفوان القرشي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5160) quotes Ibn Hibban that Abd al-Rahman ibn Safwan al-Qurashi had companionship. Via Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad from Mujahid he reports seeing the Prophet and his companions between the Black Stone and the door of the Kaaba when the Prophet entered Mecca; al-Bukhari said this is not sound. Ibn Abd al-Barr also mentions him (or Safwan ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Jumahi) asking to pledge for emigration and the reply 'No emigration after the Conquest'.
research_evidence: قال ابن حبّان: عبد الرحمن بن صفوان القرشي له صحبة. وقال ابن السكن: يقال له صحبة

full_name_ar: عبد الرحمن الخطمي والد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5119, Abd al-Rahman ibn Habib al-Khatmi) says Abu Musa (al-Madini), citing al-Khatib, stated he had companionship. Ibn Hajar says he may be the father of Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Khatmi. A separate short entry (5240) for 'Abd al-Rahman al-Khatmi' cross-refers to this one.
research_evidence: عبد الرحمن بن حبيب الخطميّ ذكر أبو موسى- عن الخطيب- أنّ له صحبة ... ويحتمل أنه والد موسى بن عبد الرحمن الخطميّ

full_name_ar: عمرو بن كعب الهمداني ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 7439) lists him as Ka'b ibn Amr ibn Musarrif al-Yami, grandfather of Ibn Musarrif, noting that he is also called Amr ibn Ka'b ibn Musarrif and that his hadith is in Abu Dawud's collection. A cross-reference entry (5958) under Amr ibn Ka'b points to this entry. The page gives the nisba al-Yami (Yam, a branch of Hamdan) rather than al-Hamdani.
research_evidence: كعب بن عمرو بن مصرف اليامي، بتحتانية باثنتين، جد ابن مصرف وقيل: هو عمرو بن كعب بن مصرف حديثه عند أبي داود

full_name_ar: عمرو بن سعد أبو سعد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5859) says Amr ibn Sa'd is said to be the name of Abu Sa'd al-Khayr, who is treated in the book's kunya section, while others give his name as Amir ibn Mas'ud. Ibn Hajar adds that Ibn al-Athir confused this person, as he explains in the book's last section.

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن مخمر ( رضي الله عنه
generation: Mukhadram / Successor — lived in the Prophet's era but is not recorded as having met him
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba has a short entry (no. 4958) for Abdullah ibn Mikhmar that only cross-refers to Abdullah ibn Muhammad in the book's last section, the section for people wrongly listed as companions. The page gives no biography, so his companion status is doubtful according to this source.

full_name_ar: عبيد بن خشخاش العنبري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5350) calls him al-Anbari of Basra; Ibn Hibban says he had companionship and Ibn al-Sakan lists him among the companions. Ibn Mandah counts him among the Bedouin of Basra and records, via Husayn ibn Abi al-Hurr, that his brother Malik and brother Qays and he came to the Prophet, who wrote them a letter of safety for their lives and property. Ibn Hajar distinguishes him from a Successor named Ubayd ibn al-Hashas who narrated from Abu Dharr.
research_evidence: عبيد بن الخشخاش العنبري البصري. قال ابن حبّان: له صحبة. وذكره أبو علي بن السكن في الصحابة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عويمر بن أبيض العجلاني ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 6129) identifies him as Uwaymir ibn Abi Abyad al-Ajlani; al-Tabarani gives his lineage as Uwaymir ibn al-Harith ibn Zayd ibn Jabir ibn al-Jadd ibn al-Ajlan, 'Abyad' being a nickname of one of his forefathers. Bukhari and Muslim record, via Sahl ibn Sa'd, that al-Ajlani asked Asim ibn Adi what a man should do who finds another man with his wife, the incident linked to the revelation of the verse of li'an (mutual cursing).
research_evidence: عويمر: بزيادة راء في آخره- هو ابن أبي أبيض العجلاني. وقال الطبراني: هو عويمر بن الحارث بن زيد بن جابر بن الجدّ بن العجلان

full_name_ar: عبادة الزرقي له صحبة ( رضي الله عنه

Ibn al-Sakan says he has only one hadith: his son Abdullah reported that Ubada took a sparrow from him, saying the Prophet made sacred what lies between Medina's two lava fields. Ibn Hajar identifies him with the son of Sa'd ibn Uthman al-Zuraqi.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7605) lists this Ma'iz with no known lineage, quoting Abu Umar (Ibn Abd al-Barr) that he has a hadith in the Musnad of Ahmad and elsewhere. The hadith concerns the Prophet being asked which deeds are best. The next entry notes that al-Bukhari and al-Baghawi treated a Ma'iz, father of 'Abdullah, as a separate person.
research_evidence: ماعز: غير منسوب. قال أبو عمر: لا أقف على نسبه، وله حديث في مسند أحمد وغيره

full_name_ar: منهال بن ملحان القيسي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 8266) lists Minhal al-Qaysi as a Companion. The entry is a brief cross-reference saying he was already mentioned under the entry of Qatada bin Milhan.
research_evidence: منهال القيسي. تقدم ذكره في قتادة بن ملحان

full_name_ar: نضلة بن نهصل الحرمازي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 8736) lists Nadla bin Tarif bin Nahshal al-Hirmazi, citing Ibn Abi 'Asim, al-Baghawi and Ibn al-Sakan. They transmitted his report via his descendant al-Junayd bin Amin bin Dharwa bin Nadla, about a dispute over a woman named Mu'adha and a poem he recited before the Prophet.
research_evidence: نضلة بن طريف: بن نهصل الحرمازي. ذكره ابن أبي عاصم والبغويّ وابن السّكن

full_name_ar: نقيرة امرأة القعقاع ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 10944, Book of Women) lists her as Buqayra (spelled with ba', not nun), wife of al-Qa'qa' bin Abi Hadrad al-Aslami.
research_evidence: بقيرة، امرأة القعقاع بن أبي حدرد الأسلمي

full_name_ar: وهب بن خنيش الطائي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9179) lists Wahb bin Khanbash, spelling the father's name with kha, nun and ba' (so Khanbash, not Khanish). It says his hadith is transmitted by al-Sha'bi, as reported by Bayan, Firas, Jabir and others; Dawud al-Awdi gave the name as Harim instead of Wahb, but Wahb is the well-known form. The entry does not state his tribe.
research_evidence: وهب بن خنبش بمعجمة ثم نون موحّدة، وزن جعفر. حديثه عند الشّعبي

full_name_ar: وهب بن عبد الله بن جنادة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9187) gives his lineage as Wahb bin 'Abdullah bin Muslim bin Junada bin Habib bin Suwa'a al-Suwa'i and identifies him as Abu Juhayfa al-Suwa'i. It says he came to the Prophet late in the Prophet's life, narrated from the Prophet, 'Ali and al-Bara' bin 'Azib, and afterwards accompanied 'Ali.
research_evidence: وهب بن عبد الله بن مسلم بن جنادة بن حبيب بن سواءة السّوائي
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: هانئ أبو مالك قدم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 8945) lists Hani' bin Malik, Abu Malik, who settled in al-Sham and was the grandfather of Khalid bin Yazid bin Abi Malik. Abu Hatim said he was a Companion; Ibn Manda reports al-Bukhari doubted his companionship. Ibn Hibban said he came to the Prophet in a delegation from Yemen and accepted Islam.
research_evidence: هانئ بن مالك الهدماني نزيل الشام، أبو مالك، وجد خالد بن يزيد بن أبي مالك. قال أبو حاتم: له صحبة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: هشام بن حبيش الخزاعي له ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Abi Hatim's al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil (entry 227) names him Hisham ibn Hubaysh ibn Khalid ibn al-Ash'ar al-Khuza'i, a Hijazi and the father of Hizam ibn Hisham, who lived at Qudayd at the foot of the Lift pass. It says he narrated from 'Umar, Suraqa ibn Malik and 'A'isha, and that his son Hizam narrated from him, citing Abu Hatim.
research_evidence: هشام بن حبيش بن خالد بن الاشعر الخزاعى حجازى والد حزام بن هشام كان ينزل قديد باصل ثنية لفت

full_name_ar: هشام بن عتبة بن زمعة القرشي ( رضي الله عنه

bio_auto: Recorded in the classical narrator registers; none of his hadith appear in the 39 collections held here. Listed among the Companions. No recorded death year survives; the timeline position is an estimate. Entry 6973 at muslimscholars.info.

full_name_ar: يزيد بن مريع الأنصاري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9328) lists Yazid bin Mirba' (spelled مربع), mentioned by Ibn Manda. It notes the report names him only as Ibn Mirba', and that his name was also said to be Zayd or 'Abdullah. Ibn Hajar suggests he may be the Awsi Ansari Companion Yazid bin Zayd bin Mirba' praised by the poet al-Shammakh bin Dirar.
research_evidence: يزيد بن مربع ذكره ابن مندة، ووقع في الخبر ابن مربع، بغير تسمية، وقيل اسمه زيد، وقيل عبد اللَّه
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: يزيد بن خارجة الأنصاري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9272) lists Yazid bin Kharija al-Ansari. The entry consists only of Ibn Hibban's statement that he was a Companion.
research_evidence: يزيد بن خارجة الأنصاريّ. قال ابن حبان: له صحبة.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: هلب والد قبيصة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9012) lists al-Hulb al-Ta'i and identifies him as Yazid bin Qunafa. Citing Ibn Durayd, it says he came to the Prophet bald, the Prophet wiped his head and hair grew, so he was called al-Hulb. His hadith appears in Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi.
research_evidence: الهلب الطائي. قال ابن دريد: أتى النبيّ صلّى اللَّه عليه وآله وسلّم رجل أقرع، فمسح رأسه فنبت شعره فسمى الهلب
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: يسار مولى رسول الله ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 9361, Yasar the shepherd) describes him as a slave of the Prophet named Yasar who was sent to look after the camels and was killed by the 'Uraniyyun. The preceding entry (9359, Yasar al-Habashi the shepherd) says Abu Nu'aym named him and cites al-Waqidi.
research_evidence: كان للنبيّ صلّى اللَّه عليه وآله وسلّم غلام يقال له يسار
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: يعمر أبو أبي خزامة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9384) lists Ya'mar, one of the Banu Sa'd bin Hudhaym and the father of Abu Khizama. The entry cites his hadith in which he asked the Prophet about the incantations (ruqa) they used for healing.
research_evidence: يعمر: أحد بني سعد بن هذيم، والد أبي خزامة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: يسير شيخ سمع النبي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: The Hadith Transmitters Encyclopedia page for Yasir quotes Ibn Hibban's al-Thiqat describing him as a shaykh who heard the Prophet say that modesty brings nothing but good. No lineage or death year is given.
research_evidence: يسير شيخ سمع النَّبِي صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُول لَا يَأْتِيك من الْحيَاء إِلَّا الْخَيْر

full_name_ar: أبو تحيا الأنصاري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9653, kunya section) lists Abu Tihya, gives the vowelling of his name, and describes him as an elder (shaykh) of the Ansar.
research_evidence: أبو تحيى بكسر المثناة وسكون المهملة وفتح التحتانية الأولى، شيخ من الأنصار.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أبو حثمة العدوي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9752) lists Abu Hathma bin Hudhayfa bin Ghanim bin 'Amir al-Qurashi al-'Adawi, brother of Abu Jahm. Citing Ibn al-Sakan, it says he was a Companion and among those who became Muslim at the Conquest of Mecca.
research_evidence: أبو حثمة بن حذيفة بن غانم بن عامر القرشي العدوي، أخو أبي جهم. قال ابن السّكن: له صحبة، وهو من مسلمة الفتح.

full_name_ar: أبو حاضر حديثه عند ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9741) lists Abu Hadir with no lineage. It says al-Baghawi, Ibn al-Jarud, al-Bawardi and Ibn Hibban counted him among the Companions, while al-Dhuhli said he did not know whether he was a Companion. Ibn Manda and al-Baghawi transmitted, via Shu'ba from Khalid al-Hadhdha' from Abu Hunayda, his report on how the Prophet prayed the funeral prayer.
research_evidence: أبو حاضر غير منسوب. ذكره البغويّ، وابن الجارود، والباورديّ، وابن حبّان في الصحابة. وقال الذهلي: لا أدري له صحبة أم لا.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أبو ليلى الخزاعي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 10481, kunya section) lists Abu Layla al-Khuza'i. It says Ibn Hibban counted him among the Companions, followed by Ja'far al-Mustaghfiri and then Abu Musa (al-Madini).
research_evidence: أبو ليلى الخزاعي. ذكره ابن حبّان في الصحابة، وتبعه جعفر المستغفري، ثم أبو موسى.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أبو هند الأشجعي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 10682, kunya section) lists Abu Hind, father of Nu'aym bin Abi Hind al-Ashja'i. The entry is a cross-reference saying he was already covered under the entry of al-Nu'man bin Ashyam.
research_evidence: أبو هند، والد نعيم بن أبي هند الأشجعي. تقدم في النعمان بن أشيم.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba lists Abu Umayya al-Ja'di among the companions with the kunya Abu Umayya (entry 9558). It refers the reader to his fuller entry under Abu Umayma (al-Jushami), noting the two names refer to the same entry.
research_evidence: أبو أمية الجعدي تقدم في أبي أميمة، وكذلك الجشمي.

full_name_ar: أم حفيد بنت الحارث بن أبي ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 11975, kunyas of women) lists Umm Hufayd bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyya, sister of Umm al-Fadl the mother of Ibn 'Abbas; her name was Huzayla. It says she is the one who gave the Prophet a gift of lizards (dabb), and refers to her fuller entry under the letter ha' among the names.
research_evidence: أم حفيظ: بفاء مصغرة، بنت الحارث الهلالية، أخت أم الفضل والدة ابن عباس. اسمها هزيلة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أم سليم بنت أبي ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 12078, kunyas of women) lists Umm Sulayman bint Abi Hakim; a separate cross-reference (entry 12072) points 'Umm Sulaym bint Hakim' to this entry. It says she is said to be the mother of Sulayman bin Abi Hathma. Citing Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr), it says she is called Umm Sulayman, also Umm Sulaym al-'Adawiyya, and by some Umm Salama.
research_evidence: أم سليمان بنت أبي حكيم: ... قال أبو عمر: أم سليمان، وقيل أم سليم العدويّة، وقال بعضهم: أم سلمة.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أم سعد بنت عمرو ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 12054) names her Umm Sa'd, also called Umm Sa'id, daughter of Murra ibn 'Amr, of Fihr or, it is said, of Jumah. It quotes Abu Umar (Ibn Abd al-Barr) giving her as bint 'Umar or 'Umayr al-Jumahiyya, notes a hadith narrated from her about the guardian of the orphan, and says its chain via Safwan is disputed.
research_evidence: أم سعد: ويقال أم سعيد، بنت مرة بن عمرو الفهريّة، ويقال الجمحيّة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

famous: Umm Abd bint al-Harith bin Yazid
full: Umm Abd bint Al-Harith bin Yazid
full_name_ar: أم عبد بنت الحارث ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 12159) lists her among the female companions as Umm 'Ubayd bint al-Harith ibn Yazid al-Hudhaliyya (spelled 'Ubayd there, with the same father and grandfather). It says only that Ja'far al-Mustaghfiri mentioned her briefly.
research_evidence: أم عبيد بنت الحارث بن يزيد الهذليّة. ذكرها جعفر المستغفري مختصرا.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أم ليلى الأنصارية ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 12240, kunyas of women) lists Umm Layla bint Rawaha al-Ansariyya, wife of Abu Layla and mother of 'Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Layla. Citing Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr), it says she was among the women who gave the pledge of allegiance and her hadith is found among the people of Kufa. Her report concerns what the women were required to observe at the pledge, including the use of henna.
research_evidence: أم ليلى: بنت رواحة الأنصاريّة. امرأة أبي ليلى، ووالدة عبد الرّحمن بن أبي ليلى.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أم معاذ الأنصارية ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba has two entries named Umm Mu'adh al-Ansariyya on this page (12260 and 12261). Entry 12260 says she is mentioned in Umm 'Atiyya's hadith about the women's pledge not to wail, as one of the few women who kept it (with Umm Sulaym and Umm al-'Ala'). Entry 12261 cites Ibn Manda and Ibn Sa'd that she accepted Islam and gave the pledge; Ibn Hajar raises the possibility that the reports concern the same woman.
research_evidence: ١٢٢٦٠- أم معاذ الأنصارية: وقع ذكرها في حديث أم عطية بالبيعة على ألا ينحن. قالت: فما وفت منا امرأة إلا أم سليم
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: أم المنذر العدوية ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Entry 12273 in Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba, an Ansari woman whose lineage runs through 'Adi bin al-Najjar (the page itself does not use the word al-'Adawiyya). Citing al-Tabarani, her name was Salma bint Qays, sister of Salit bin Qays. The entry continues on https://shamela.ws/book/9767/4394 with her hadith about the Prophet visiting her with 'Ali, recorded by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and Ibn Sa'd via Fulayh bin Sulayman.
research_evidence: ١٢٢٧٣- أم المنذر بنت قيس بن عمرو [بن عبيد] بن عامر بن غنم بن عدي بن النّجّار الأنصاريّة النّجّارية
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: الورد بن خالد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Entry 9140 in Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba, of the tribe of Sulaym. Citing Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr, al-Isti'ab), he was on the Prophet's right flank at the Conquest of Mecca. The editor's notes also reference Usd al-Ghaba.
research_evidence: ورد بن خالد بن حذيفة بن عمرو بن خلف بن مازن بن مالك بن ثعلبة ابن بهثة بن سليم السلميّ البجلي
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن نعيم الأشجعي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Entry 5011 in Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba. Citing Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi, he was the Prophet's guide on the way to Khaybar; Ibn Hajar notes al-Baghawi gave no chain for this, and that al-Tabari also mentioned him.
research_evidence: عبد الله بن نعيم الأشجعي ذكره أبو القاسم البغويّ في الصحابة، وقال: كان دليل النبيّ صلى اللَّه عليه وسلّم، إلى خيبر
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عامر بن الأضبط الأشجعي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Entry 4381 in Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba. Ibn Hajar says Ibn Shahin and others mentioned him and related a story indicating he was killed at the time he accepted Islam, before he met the Prophet.
research_evidence: عامر بن الأضبط الأشجعيّ. ذكره ابن شاهين وغيره، وساق قصّة تدلّ على أنه قتل حين أسلم قبل أن يلقى النّبي صلّى اللَّه عليه وسلم
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: ناجية بن الأعجم الأسلمي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Entry 8662 in Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba. Ibn Sa'd lists him among the companions and says he left no descendants; al-Waqidi reports he went down into the well at al-Hudaybiyya with the Prophet's arrow to increase its water (others attribute this to Najiya bin Jundab). A report says the Prophet gave him one of two standards on the day of the Conquest of Mecca, and Ibn Shahin says he died in Medina late in the caliphate of Mu'awiya.
research_evidence: ناجية: بن الأعجم الأسلميّ. ذكره ابن سعد في الصّحابة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن وهب الأسلمي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Entry 5043 in Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba, citing Ibn Sa'd, al-Baghawi, al-Waqidi's Kitab al-Ridda and al-Tabari. He was in Oman with 'Amr bin al-'As when the Prophet died and was intercepted by Musaylima; one report says he outwardly followed Musaylima out of fear after his companion was burned, and Usama bin Zayd stopped 'Abbas bin Abi Rabi'a from killing him at al-Yamama. He later accompanied Khalid bin al-Walid against the apostates.
research_evidence: عبد اللَّه بن وهب الأسلمي: له صحبة. ذكره ابن سعد والبغوي، وكان عند وفاة النبيّ صلى اللَّه عليه وسلّم بعمان مع عمرو بن العاص
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عمرو بن حمزة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Entry 5833 in Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba, where the name is given as 'Amr bin Abi Hamza bin Sinan al-Aslami (with 'Abi'). Citing al-Waqidi via al-Mundhir bin Jahm, he was present at al-Hudaybiyya with the Prophet; the entry also relates that he later confessed a transgression to the Prophet.
research_evidence: ٥٨٣٣ ز- عمرو بن أبي حمزة بن سنان الأسلمي. ذكر الواقديّ من طريق المنذر بن جهم، عن عمرو بن أبي حمزة هذا أنه شهد الحديبيّة مع رسول اللَّه صلى اللَّه عليه وسلّم
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عمرو بن عبد نهم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Entry 5917 in Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba. Citing Ibn 'Abd al-Barr, he guided the Prophet on the route on the day of al-Hudaybiyya; Ibn Hajar adds that this is doubtful, since Ibn Shahin's report of it comes through a weak chain.
research_evidence: ٥٩١٧- عمرو بن عبد نهم الأسلمي : ذكره ابن عبد البرّ، وقال: هو الّذي دلّ رسول اللَّه صلى اللَّه عليه وسلّم على الطريق يوم الحديبيّة

research_evidence: ٤٥٤٩- عبد اللَّه بن الأسود السدوسي بن شعبة بن علقمة بن شهاب بن عوف بن عمرو بن الحارث بن سدوس السدوسي
